272.h: Federal University, Wukari (FUWukari) was established in 2011 by the Federal Government under President Goodluck Jonathan, as one of the nine new federal universities created that year.
272.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
272.c: It is located in the town of Wukari in southern Taraba State, north-eastern Nigeria.

273.h: Godfrey Okoye University (GO University) belongs to the Catholic Diocese of Enugu and was the first university in Africa to be owned by a Catholic diocese. It was founded by Very Reverend Father Professor Christian Anieke and received its operating licence from the National Universities Commission on 3 November 2009. It started that year with 215 students and had admitted 1,200 by the end of 2012. Its first convocation took place in December 2013.
273.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes.
273.c: The university is located in Enugu, the capital of Enugu State.

274.h: Gombe State University (GSU) is a public university owned by the Gombe State Government, established in 2004. Its first vice-chancellor was Professor Abdullahi Mahadi. The university is governed by a council of eleven members under its chancellor.
274.a: GSU offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, and is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities.
274.c: The campus is at Tudun Wada, in the Shamaki ward of Gombe, the capital of Gombe State.

275.h: Greenfield University is a private university in Kaduna, established in January 2019. It began its first academic session in May 2019. In April 2021 the university was the target of a mass kidnapping of students, one of a series of attacks on schools in northern Nigeria at the time.
275.a: The university began with three faculties: Social and Management Sciences, Engineering, and Science and Technology.
275.c: It is located in Kaduna State, in north-western Nigeria.

276.h: Gregory University, Uturu (GUU) is a private university named after Pope Gregory I. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2012.
276.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
276.c: It is located in Uturu, Abia State, in south-eastern Nigeria.

277.h: Hallmark University is a private university established by the Vivian Fowler Trust Foundation, the organisation behind Vivian Fowler Memorial College in Lagos, and approved by the Federal Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2015.
277.a: The university offers more than 18 degree programmes across the sciences, management and the social sciences. Candidates must be at least 16 years old at the start of the session.
277.c: The campus is at Ijebu-Itele in Ogun State.

278.h: Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University, Lapai (IBBUL) is a public university owned by the Niger State Government and named after General Ibrahim Babangida, a former head of state who comes from Niger State. It began academic activities in the 2005/2006 session and held its first convocation in 2014.
278.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
278.c: It is located in Lapai, Niger State, in central Nigeria.

279.h: Igbinedion University, Okada is a private university founded by Chief Gabriel Igbinedion. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 1999, which places it among the first private universities licensed in Nigeria.
279.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, law and engineering.
279.c: It is located in Okada, a town in Ovia North-East, Edo State. Students live and study on a residential campus.

280.h: Ignatius Ajuru University of Education (IAUE) is a public university owned by the Rivers State Government and devoted to the training of teachers. The National Universities Commission records its establishment as a university in 2010; it grew out of the former Rivers State College of Education.
280.a: IAUE awards degrees in education across arts, sciences, social sciences and vocational subjects, preparing graduates to teach in Nigerian schools.
280.c: The university is located in Port Harcourt, the capital of Rivers State.

281.h: Imo State University (IMSU) is a public university owned by the Imo State Government. It was first established in 1981 under Law No. 4 of the Imo State House of Assembly, and admitted 392 pioneer students on 23 October 1981. When Abia State was created in 1991, the original Uturu campus became Abia State University, and Imo State University was re-established in Owerri; the National Universities Commission records this as 1992.
281.a: Most IMSU programmes have full accreditation from the National Universities Commission. The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees, including medicine.
281.c: The university is located in Owerri, the capital of Imo State.

282.h: Kaduna State University (KASU) is a public university owned by the Kaduna State Government, established in 2004.
282.a: KASU has sixteen faculties and more than 50 departments.
282.c: It has two main campuses, in Kaduna city and in Kafanchan in southern Kaduna State.

284.h: Karl Kumm University (KKU) is a private Christian university established by the Sudan United Mission, a missionary organisation founded in 1904 by the German missionary Karl Kumm, after whom the university is named. The university gives 2017 for its founding, and the National Universities Commission records 2021.
284.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
284.c: It is located in Vom, Plateau State, near Jos.

285.h: Kebbi State University of Science and Technology (KSUSTA) is a public university owned by the Kebbi State Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2006, and it was the 79th university in Nigeria.
285.a: KSUSTA focuses on agriculture and the sciences, among other programmes.
285.c: It is located in Aliero, Kebbi State, in north-western Nigeria.

286.h: Kings University is a private university founded in 2015 by the Kingsway International Christian Centre, the church led by Pastor Matthew Ashimolowo, who serves as the university's chancellor.
286.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
286.c: It is located at Ode-Omu in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.

287.h: Kogi State University, now named Prince Abubakar Audu University (PAAU), is a public university owned by the Kogi State Government. It was established in 1999 during the administration of Governor Abubakar Audu, and was renamed in his honour in 2020 by Governor Yahaya Bello. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Professor S. K. Okwute, a chemist, who served from 2000 to 2005.
287.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
287.c: It is located in Anyigba, Kogi State.

288.h: Kwara State University (KWASU) is a public research university owned by the Kwara State Government. It was established in 2009 by the administration of Governor Bukola Saraki and was designed from the start to emphasise community service and entrepreneurship as well as teaching and research.
288.a: KWASU has about 60 academic departments in 11 faculties.
288.c: The university is located at Malete, near Ilorin, in Kwara State.

289.h: Kwararafa University, Wukari is a private university established in 2005 and accredited by the National Universities Commission. Its name recalls the historic Kwararafa confederacy of the Jukun people, centred on the Wukari area.
289.c: It is located in Wukari, Taraba State.

290.h: Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH) is a public research university, established in 1990 and named after Samuel Ladoke Akintola, a former premier of the Western Region who came from Ogbomoso. It was jointly owned by Oyo and Osun States for many years and is now owned by Oyo State.
290.a: LAUTECH is a large university with more than 30,000 students and over 3,000 staff. Its programmes focus on engineering, technology, the sciences, agriculture and medicine.
290.c: The main campus is in Ogbomoso, Oyo State.

291.h: Lagos State University of Education (LASUED) is a public university owned by the Lagos State Government and dedicated to teacher education. The National Universities Commission records its establishment as a university in 2022; it was formed from the state's former colleges of education.
291.a: LASUED trains teachers for a wide range of school subjects, from English, mathematics and the sciences to Nigerian languages, social studies and vocational subjects. Admission requires credit passes in English Language and Mathematics, together with subjects relevant to the chosen course.
291.c: The main campus is at Ijanikin, Lagos State.

292.h: Lagos State University of Science and Technology (LASUSTECH) is a public institution owned by the Lagos State Government. It began as Lagos State College of Science and Technology, became Lagos State Polytechnic, and was upgraded to a university; the National Universities Commission records this as 2022.
292.a: The university concentrates on science, engineering and technology programmes.
292.c: It is located in Ikorodu, Lagos State.

293.h: Landmark University is a private Christian university affiliated with the Living Faith Church Worldwide, the church that also founded Covenant University. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2011.
293.a: Landmark is known for its emphasis on agriculture alongside engineering, the sciences and business. In 2014 it was placed among the top five universities in Nigeria by the Webometrics ranking.
293.c: The campus is at Omu-Aran in Kwara State.

294.h: Lead City University (LCU) is a private university in Ibadan. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2005.
294.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and law.
294.c: It is located in Ibadan, the capital of Oyo State.
